It often comes down to body composition — muscle generates more heat than fat, so people with less muscle mass (often women, on average, due to hormonal differences) tend to feel cold more easily. Circulation plays a role too — smaller blood vessels in hands and feet constrict faster to preserve core body temperature, sacrificing your fingers and toes first as a defense mechanism. So “always cold” people aren’t being dramatic, their bodies are just prioritizing survival organs over comfort.

Fun fact: Breaking Bad originally planned for Walter White to have a full head of hair, but Bryan Cranston suggested shaving it to make Walter’s appearance feel more severe as he entered the drug world.

The series follows Walter, a chemistry teacher who begins manufacturing methamphetamine with former student Jesse Pinkman after being diagnosed with cancer.

One interesting detail is that the show’s opening title contains chemical element symbols, including Br for bromine and Ba for barium, reinforcing the chemistry theme from the very first seconds.

Another cool fact is that many of the desert scenes were filmed around Albuquerque, New Mexico, and the city became so closely linked to the series that fans still visit its filming locations.

That mix of hidden details, unforgettable performances, and Walter White’s complete transformation is what made Breaking Bad one of television’s most rewatchable dramas. 🧪🚐⚠️
